name: Gorilla Biscuits
label: Revelation
lede: Queens kids named after a slang word for quaaludes made the most joyful straight edge record ever pressed, and it turned into the best-selling thing Revelation has ever put out.

eras.title: A joke name out of Queens
eras.text: Three friends from the same Queens high school started a band with a name they figured they'd drop. Then Walter Schreifels came in with a stack of songs, and the joke name was stuck to the most tuneful band in New York hardcore.

years.p: [[Anthony "Civ" Civarelli|a5d69704-924b-4128-9577-e16531503890]], [[Arthur Smilios|40d4f905-3bb1-4d2e-9a9b-1d7891033094]] and Nick Drysdale start the band in Queens. The name comes from street slang for quaaludes, the pills big enough to be called gorilla biscuits. It was meant to be temporary.

Already playing bass in [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], Schreifels takes guitar and becomes the songwriter. [[Luke Abbey|6ab9b327-0f98-4515-907c-13078f426cc5]] settles in on drums.

Gorilla Biscuits come up in the same all-ages New York crowd as Youth of Today, [[Side By Side|8dc812b1-d387-4c45-8173-f0d5bd0c318f]] and [[Bold|b024b1bd-2020-4b7c-83f7-4660133c89fa]], the circle that Revelation Records starts documenting that year.

eras.title: Seven songs and a lost tape
eras.text: The first record was eleven and a half minutes of hooks, cut in one January session with Don Fury. It sold well enough that Revelation kept pressing it, which is when they discovered the master was gone.

years.src: Revelation Records pressing history · Wikipedia: Gorilla Biscuits (album)
years.p: Seven Schreifels songs recorded at Demo Demo Studios in New York, produced by Schreifels and [[Don Fury|0bec484f-b890-4823-af64-0e48530f6f6f]]. It runs 11:35.
years.xp:
Collectors know the first press by the 102 copies with blank white and yellow labels, stamped by hand with the band's name.

After that first run the master tape went missing. Revelation had to remix the EP for every pressing that followed, so the earliest copies are the only ones that sound exactly like the session.

years.p: A second guitarist fills out the sound in time for the full-length.

eras.title: Start Today
eras.text: Recorded over four months and released on Revelation, Start Today took the youth crew template and made it sing. It became the label's biggest seller and the record most people mean when they talk about the sound of late-'80s New York straight edge.

years.cap: Start Today, Revelation 1989. The first pressing came in an embossed cover
years.src: Revelation Records pressing history · Wikipedia: Start Today
years.p: Tracked at Demo² Studios from January to April, produced by the band and Don Fury. Every song is Schreifels' except a [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] cover. New Direction opens it.
years.xp:
The first pressing came in an embossed cover. The seal on the shrink wrap ran top to bottom on the purple vinyl copies and left to right on the black ones, the kind of detail Rev's own pressing notes still track.

It went on to pass 100,000 CD copies, Revelation's best seller, and NME later put it among the fifteen best hardcore albums ever made.

years.p: Nazi skinheads were turning up at shows, some throwing salutes during sets. The band's answer was to play its anti-racist song straight at them. Civ later said standing onstage talking unity meant putting yourself on the line.

eras.title: Everybody's in two bands
eras.text: The Revelation circle was small, and by 1990 the same handful of players was powering half its roster. Gorilla Biscuits toured on borrowed friends, then quietly came apart as Schreifels and Civ followed new ideas.

years.p: The Youth of Today drummer replaces Abbey. On the 1990 European tour Porcell comes along too, so it's close to a Youth of Today reunion with Civ singing.
Heavier, slower and aimed somewhere past hardcore. It would soon take most of his time.

years.h: The EP comes back on CD, twelve songs long
years.p: Revelation's CD adds the Buzzcocks cover, two new originals and demo versions, stretching the 7" to nearly twenty minutes.
No farewell record. Civ goes on to front [[CIV|1649c891-eea0-45b2-8caf-c85d985ff3bd]], a band built largely from Gorilla Biscuits players.

eras.title: Back at the matinee
eras.text: The reunions began as favors to their own scene: a benefit at CBGB, then a return to the room before it closed for good. Over the next decade Gorilla Biscuits became one of hardcore's most dependable reunion draws, on both sides of the Atlantic.

years.p: The band reunites at a benefit for the late [[Warzone|496da466-68e9-4cbb-9e86-cbb57eda861a]] singer, with Alex Brown back on guitar.
The reunion that sticks, at the Bowery club a year before it shut its doors.

years.h: At the Matinee: twenty copies a night
years.p: A self-released record with two new songs, sold only at shows, twenty copies per tour stop.
A European tour, the first since the Siegler-and-Porcell run of 1990.
A Manhattan headliner in the old East Village ballroom.
Part of the label's three-night anniversary run in California.
Revelation opens preorders for a silver anniversary pressing, and brings back the Jungle T-shirt.

eras.title: A speech and a loss
eras.text: The band that sang about unity got pulled into a fight over what unity means in 2016. Three years later it lost the guitarist who had been there since 1988.

q: My name is attached to trigger phrases that never left my mouth.
years.p: At This Is Hardcore in Philadelphia, Civ introduces the anti-racist song by saying people shouldn't still need shirts that say Black Lives Matter, and that everyone matters. Critics hear an All Lives Matter line.
years.xp:
The backlash was quick and loud across punk media. Civ's side: he meant that a basic truth shouldn't need a slogan on a shirt, and he pointed to decades of songs about unity and against judging people.

His critics' side: at that moment, recasting Black Lives Matter as everybody matters was exactly the move the movement was pushing back against. The argument never fully resolved.

years.p: The band's guitarist since 1988 dies. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]], Civ's guitarist in CIV, takes his place.
